reviews.reasons: Opening choice and stance are right: the form-pack listing has every link evidenced on its own record (93 sales at $29 from 3,100 unique visitors in the last 30 days = 3.0%, traffic stable within 10% for three months, Brain produces the spreadsheet, $3 cost, cash in 3 days, 0 owner hours), and the walkthrough is correctly excluded (8 owner hours each vs 6 owner hours in the window; the target needs 24). But the ledger timing contradicts the evidence the plan cites. At 3,100 visitors per 30 days the listing gets ~103 visitors/day, and at 3.0% that is ~3.1 sales/day. The plan books all 45 sales on day 3 and all 45 receipts on day 4 (settling day 7, proof day 10); 45 sales need ~1,500 visitors, i.e. ~14.5 days of traffic, not 3. By day 10 only ~31 sales (~$900) are expected, so the proof condition as scheduled would read as a failure on a plan that is actually on track. Recomputed correctly: 42 sales reach $1,200 ($1,218); sales through day 18 settle by day 21: ~1,860 visitors x 3% = ~56 expected sales (~$1,620 gross, sd ~7 sales), so the target is reached in the window with margin. Revise the cash ledger to accrue ~3 sales/day (receipts settling 3 days after each sale), put the proof day near day 17-18 (when ~42 sales have settled), and keep EXECUTABLE.

reviews.reasons: The ledger now matches the measured rate: 3,100 visitors/30 days = ~103/day x 3.0% = ~3.1 sales/day. Tranches recomputed: days 1-7 = ~21.7 expected, booked 21 x $29 = $609 settling day 10; days 8-14 booked 21 = $609 settling day 17; cumulative 42 sales = $1,218 >= $1,200 settled by day 17 (proof day 17). Days 15-18 are counted conservatively at 3 of ~12 expected ($87, settling day 21). Total collected $1,305 in window. Costs ($3 per sale, $135 total) are spent on each tranche's settlement day from receipts, so no owner funding; zero owner hours vs 2 h/week. Checkout, delivery and payout now run through the existing listing, matching the card's channel. Every link is evidenced on this listing's own analytics and sales report; EXECUTABLE is right. The walkthrough exclusion stands on the owner-hours limit (8 h each vs 6 h in the window).
findings: Margin: by day 17 the plan needs 42 sales from ~1,750 visitors of traffic through day 14 (expected ~43); the target at day 17 is close to the expectation, but sales through day 18 (expected ~56) all settle by day 21, so the day-21 proof has ~14 sales of slack (~2 sd).
Traffic is measured stable within 10% for three months; a 10% traffic dip still leaves ~50 expected sales through day 18, above the 42 needed.
